title: Father, United by Thy Grace
description: Father, United by Thy Grace in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 45, “Made Perfect in Love”, where the book credits them to Methodist.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther, u-ni-ted by Thy grace, And each to each en-deared, With con-fi-dence we seek Thy face, And know our prayer is heard.

lines: With confidence we seek Thy face,
And know our prayer is heard.
Touched by the loadstone of Thy love,
And ever towards each other move,
Grant this, and then from all below
Our souls their change shall scarcely know,
To us the ministry be given,
For love can make on earth a heaven,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
